name: Player Digging
desc: Player starts/cancels/ends mining a block, or drops an item (press Q).

fields.name: facing
fields.desc: Face of the block being mined

fields.name: status
fields.desc: START_DESTROY_BLOCK, ABORT_DESTROY_BLOCK, STOP_DESTROY_BLOCK, DROP_ALL_ITEMS, DROP_ITEM, RELEASE_USE_ITEM

notes: RELEASE_USE_ITEM (5) is used when the player stops eating/drinking/using a bow.

writeup.p: C07PacketPlayerDigging is the serverbound mining and item-use control channel. The wire form is a packed BlockPos (long), a facing byte, and a status enum byte: START_DESTROY_BLOCK, ABORT_DESTROY_BLOCK, STOP_DESTROY_BLOCK, DROP_ALL_ITEMS, DROP_ITEM, RELEASE_USE_ITEM. It is the only way the server learns that the player began mining, finished or cancelled a dig, dropped an item, or released a use-item action such as a bow draw, eating, or blocking. Client-side it is emitted from PlayerControllerMP.clickBlock (START), onPlayerDamageBlock (ABORT), onPlayerDestroyBlock (STOP), EntityPlayerSP.dropOneItem (DROP) and PlayerControllerMP.onStoppedUsingItem (RELEASE_USE_ITEM).

NetHandlerPlayServer.processPlayerDigging switches on the status. DROP_ITEM and DROP_ALL_ITEMS call dropOneItem(false/true) unless the player is a spectator. RELEASE_USE_ITEM calls stopUsingItem, which ends the bow draw or eating and computes the fired arrow or consumed food server-side. The three dig actions share a distance gate: squared distance from the player to the block center (with a +1.5 Y bias) must be under 36.0 and the block Y below the build limit. START calls ItemInWorldManager.tryHarvestBlock when the block is not protected and inside the world border, otherwise the server replies with an S23 block change. STOP calls onPlayerDestroyBlock and ABORT cancels the dig; after STOP or ABORT an S23 is re-sent if the block is not air. There is no per-action rate limit.

Four families dominate the corpus. Mining automation: Nuker in Rise 5.99 and 6.x sends START+STOP pairs around every block in a radius, with Teleport and Area modes that walk to the target first; Breaker in Memeware, Rise 5.99 and the Rise 6.x Breaker/NewBreaker/NewNewBreaker suite destroys cake, beds and targeted blocks; Tenacity's SpeedMine accumulates block damage client-side and finishes the dig itself. Item-use automation: FastBow in Memeware, Rise 5.99 and Sigma fires fully charged arrows by releasing early; the Rise 5.99 AutoGap/AutoPot/AutoHead/AutoSoup family and Sigma's FastUse use RELEASE_USE_ITEM to end eating, potting and item use instantly. NoSlow lives in Memeware, Rise 5.99, Rise 6.x (Legit/NCP/Intave), Sigma and Spicy, pairing RELEASE_USE_ITEM with a C08 re-place to cancel the slow. Combat auras in every client use RELEASE_USE_ITEM for autoblock, and Rise 6.x velocity and disabler modules spoof dig state for anti-cheat bypasses.

The server processes a START+STOP pair as a complete break with no client-side damage accounting, so any module can mine instantly at the packet level; the only server-side evidence is the block's hardness versus the reported dig duration. RELEASE_USE_ITEM ignores the BlockPos entirely, so Spicy's NoSlow can send it with a random double-range position and the server reads only the status. The 36.0 distance gate is generous versus the client's 6-block reach, and Teleport-mode Nuker satisfies it by walking before digging. DROP_ITEM is a free inventory channel. Anti-cheats counter with dig-speed measurement (hardness versus START-to-STOP gap), per-second block counts for nuker patterns, and the release+re-place gap for NoSlow.

implementation.overview: The mining and item-use control packet: six status values over a packed position and facing byte. Nuker and Breaker forge START+STOP pairs for instant mining, Tenacity's SpeedMine runs the block math client-side, FastBow releases the bow early through RELEASE_USE_ITEM, and NoSlow pairs the release with a C08 re-place to cancel eating and blocking slows. Autoblock auras in every client fire RELEASE_USE_ITEM around each attack.
implementation.server_handling: processPlayerDigging resolves the block position, then switches on the status ordinal. Drop actions skip the distance check entirely and go straight to dropOneItem; the spectator gate is the only guard. RELEASE_USE_ITEM also skips position validation and calls stopUsingItem, which is why the random-position trick works: the server reads the enum and nothing else. Dig actions enforce the 36.0 squared-distance gate with the +1.5 Y bias, the build-limit clamp, the world-border check and the block-protection check (an S23 is sent back when the dig is refused). STOP_DESTROY_BLOCK is what actually breaks the block via onPlayerDestroyBlock; START only enters the mining state. The ItemInWorldManager tracks the dig progress server-side, but a module that sends START then STOP back-to-back completes the state machine in one round trip.
implementation.protocol_notes: The BlockPos is packed into a single long as ((x & 0x3FFFFFF) << 38) | ((y & 0xFFF) << 26) | (z & 0x3FFFFFF). The facing byte and the status byte follow; MCP reads both via readEnumValue, so both are VarInts on the wire. Status ordinals: 0 START_DESTROY_BLOCK, 1 ABORT_DESTROY_BLOCK, 2 STOP_DESTROY_BLOCK, 3 DROP_ALL_ITEMS, 4 DROP_ITEM, 5 RELEASE_USE_ITEM. Drop packets conventionally use BlockPos.ORIGIN with EnumFacing.DOWN; modules copy that convention even for release packets, and Spicy's NoSlow deliberately breaks it with random coordinates. The packet is registered at 0x07 in the SERVERBOUND play state table.
implementation.anticheat_landscape: NCP and Matrix measure the START-to-STOP gap against the block's hardness and flag instant breaks; Nuker patterns are caught by counting unique blocks destroyed per second, which is why Rise 5.99's Nuker ships a Tick throttle and an Instant Only mode that refuses hardness above 0. SpeedMine avoids the dig-speed flag by never lying about the gap: it finishes the client-side damage model and only then sends STOP. NoSlow is detected by the release+re-place packet pattern and by position comparison on the C07, which is what Spicy's random BlockPos defeats. GrimVelocity and StandardVelocity in Rise 6.x spoof START/STOP to satisfy mining-state checks during knockback, and the CubeCraft and Vulcan disablers send STOP/START at the player's own position to reset server dig state. The item-use family (FastBow, FastUse) is flagged by charge-time measurement between the C08 use and the C07 release.

modules.name: Nuker
modules.purpose: Break every block in a radius cube by sending START+STOP pairs at the packet level, with teleport and area variants.
modules.how_it_works: On update, every N ticks, iterate the radius-minus-1 cube; skip air and, in Instant Only mode, any block with hardness above 0; send START_DESTROY_BLOCK then STOP_DESTROY_BLOCK for each target via sendPacketWithoutEvent, with an optional swing. Teleport mode ray-traces 999 blocks on use, pathfinds to the target with C04 packets, nukes, and walks back; Area mode picks a random point inside the .setarea box. An S02 chat filter cancels the plot-protection message.
modules.vanilla_hook: UpdateEvent for the dig loop; PacketReceiveEvent for the chat cancel.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Instant START+STOP on high-hardness blocks is the canonical nuker flag; the Tick throttle bounds blocks-per-tick and Instant Only bounds the tell. The Teleport mode trips movement checks if the C04 walk is not replayed, so the pathfinding round trip doubles as the anti-movement-check measure.
modules.variations: Rise 6.1.30 and 6.2.4 ship the same module but send only START_DESTROY_BLOCK and rely on the client's own PlayerControllerMP loop to finish the dig, trading instant breaks for a subtler packet stream.

modules.name: Breaker
modules.purpose: Destroy specific blocks (cake, beds, wool, end stone) in a radius for bedwars-style play.
modules.how_it_works: Memeware's Breaker, registered as BlockFucker, scans a 5-block cube every update and, when the block is cake or end stone, sends START then STOP with EnumFacing.NORTH via sendPacketSilent. The target list is a BlockSelectionSetting defaulting to cake, bed, wool and end stone; the pickaxeSlot, cakeBesideOrAt and cakeCovered helpers are dead code left in the file.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Same instant-break surface as Nuker; on bedwars servers the flag is per-block-count rather than hardness, since cake and beds are already low-hardness. The silent send path keeps the pairs off the event bus so no other module reacts.
modules.variations: Rise 5.99's Breaker sends START+STOP with EnumFacing.UP and more target configuration. Rise 6.x carries three generations: Breaker and NewBreaker (START+STOP, EnumFacing.UP) and NewNewBreaker (EnumFacing.DOWN, with block-state tracking before the dig).

modules.name: SpeedMine
modules.purpose: Mine faster by running the block-breaking math client-side and finishing the dig with a single STOP packet.
modules.how_it_works: On PacketSendEvent it arms on START_DESTROY_BLOCK, records position and facing, and disarms on ABORT or STOP. While armed, every pre-motion tick accumulates damage += playerRelativeBlockHardness * speed; when damage reaches 1 it swaps the block to air client-side and sends STOP_DESTROY_BLOCK via sendPacketNoEvent. blockHitDelay is zeroed so the next block starts immediately.
modules.vanilla_hook: PacketSendEvent for the dig state machine; MotionEvent pre for damage accumulation.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The server receives a legitimately timed STOP, so dig-speed checks that measure the START-to-STOP gap see a plausible duration; the client-side air swap is invisible to the server, which only ever sees the completed break. Anti-cheats that simulate hardness independently still flag the effective speed multiplier.
modules.variations: No other client in the corpus implements client-side damage accumulation for this packet; Memeware, Rise and Sigma achieve speed mining purely through packet pairs or by letting PlayerControllerMP run.

modules.name: NoSlowdown / NoSlow
modules.purpose: Cancel the movement slow applied while eating or blocking by releasing the use-item state and immediately re-placing.
modules.how_it_works: Spicy's NoSlow, on pre update while blocking with a sword, moving, on ground within 0.42 and with no killaura target, sends RELEASE_USE_ITEM with a BlockPos built from RandomUtils.nextDouble(4.9E-324D, 1.7976931348623157E308D) on every axis, then on post sends C08PacketPlayerBlockPlacement at (-1,-1,-1) with the held item to re-enter the block state. The server reads only the status of the release, so the random position is harmless to vanilla but defeats position-comparing heuristics.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The release+re-place pair is the detectable pattern: anti-cheats measure the gap between the C07 release and the C08 place, and some compare the C07 position to the player's location, which the random BlockPos defeats. LegitNoSlow in Rise 6.x deliberately mirrors vanilla timing to minimize the gap signature.
modules.variations: Memeware's NoSlow is the same release-plus-place pattern. Rise 5.99's NoSlow sends RELEASE_USE_ITEM pairs from its packet handler. Rise 6.x splits LegitNoSlow (watches C07 releases and replays the C08), NCPNoSlow and IntaveNoSlow. Sigma's NoSlowdown sends RELEASE_USE_ITEM on a timer.

modules.name: FastBow
modules.purpose: Fire fully charged arrows without holding the draw, by releasing the use-item state early and faking the charge.
modules.how_it_works: While the use key is held with a bow, reset the item damage to -1, call sendUseItem to enter the use state, then send 20 C06PacketPlayerPosLook packets aimed at the target with onGround true so the server registers continuous rotation during the charge. Fire RELEASE_USE_ITEM, then call onPlayerStoppedUsing directly with a charge tick of 10, which fixes the arrow power as a 10-tick draw regardless of real draw time. A trailing bare C03 keeps the movement stream alive.
modules.vanilla_hook: UpdateEvent pre; the release goes through addToSendQueue, the item callback is invoked directly.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Charge-time checks measure the gap between the C08 use and the C07 release; a sub-tick gap with a full-power arrow is the tell. The 20 look packets also fake an aiming window for rotation checks. The duraHack windowClick double-swap is a separate durability exploit and a visible inventory-packet pattern.
modules.variations: Rise 5.99's FastBow sends C04 y-0.5 and C06 look packets before the release. Sigma's FastBow sends C04 offset pairs plus RELEASE_USE_ITEM through addToSendQueue.

implementation.general_hooks: Dig and drop automation hooks UpdateEvent or MotionEvent and sends C07 directly. Item-use and NoSlow modules hook the same events but split pre and post phases: release on pre, re-place on post. Packet-listener modules (Tenacity SpeedMine, Rise 6.x LegitNoSlow, Sigma Scaffold, Rise Infinite) instead hook the outgoing packet event and inspect getStatus() to react to the vanilla dig state machine.
implementation.client_variations: Send paths: PacketUtil.sendPacket and sendPacketSilent in Memeware, addToSendQueue in Nekoware and Tenacity, PacketUtil.sendPacket and sendPacketWithoutEvent in Rise 5.99, PacketUtil.send and sendNoEvent in Rise 6.x, addToSendQueue and NetworkManager.sendPacketNoEvent in Sigma and Spicy. Rise 5.99 and 6.x also expose C07 to their scripting APIs (PacketAPI.send with Action.valueOf). The facing byte varies by module: EnumFacing.UP for nuker and breaker floods, EnumFacing.DOWN for release and drop packets, EnumFacing.NORTH in Memeware's Breaker.
